messages.subject: [rkward-users] Error when trying to load an .R file in clicking on it
messages.subject_clean: [rkward-users] Error when trying to load an .R file in clicking on it
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

sorry for the long delay.

On Tuesday 28 February 2012, Francois Maurice wrote:
> I'd like to be able to load a script file directly when I clic on it but
> the following error message appears : 
> Error loading workspace - RKWard
> There has been an error opening file
>  'J:/dossiers/Francois/Cours/COURS.E10/SOL6021/Programmation/R/Analyse.R':
>  
> Is there a way to do that ?

RKWard tries to open a file passed on the command line as a workspace, not as a 
script file. This may be improved in the future, but currently that's the way 
it is. It is possible to work around this, although on Windows that's quite 
cumbersome:

1. Create a .bat file with the following content:

REM opens command line argument as a script file in RKWard
SET file=%1
SET file=%file:\=/%
C:\RKWard\KDE\bin\rkward.bat --evaluate rk.edit.files('%file%')

(NOTE: Replace c:\RKWard\KDE\bin\rkward.bat with the correct path to 
rkward.bat on your system).

2. Change the file type association of .R files from rkward to the .bat file you 
created.

Now, clicking a .R file should start an RKWard session, and run the command
  rk.edit.files('FILENAME')
in it, automatically. Note that each .R file will open in a separate rkward 
session.

I hope that helps a bit.

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] Bravo
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Thursday 08 March 2012, Francois Maurice wrote:
> RKWard is the best R GUI available. Really nice job and it is a lot of job.
> It is also serious job. I'll try to participate to the development of
> RKWard in a near future.

thanks for the flattery, and I'm very much looking forward to your 
participiation. Please note that I do not have a whole lot of time for the 
project at the moment (I hope that will improve again, soon). Just so you know 
that if you don't get feedback immediately, that's not for a lack of interest.

> The biggest drawback is the dependence of RKWard
> on KDE. KDE is heavy and not so easy to install. But hey, I guess KDE has
> advantages.

Yes, one of the key advantages is the text editor component. Also KDE is 
currently working on becoming more modular, so the KDE dependency will 
hopefully become less heavy in the not-too-distant future.

> Perhaps we are due for a simple and elegant website to better
> promote RKWard, something like the Web site of RStudio. 

The website is definitely in need of some love. As you can see this is 
currently based on a wiki, to reduce the maintenance effort. But even within 
this framework, a lot can certainly be done both about content and design. I 
have just given you editor rights in the wiki, so you can start working on 
improvements. Of course, for larger changes, and esp. for changes to central 
pages, please do your work on a temporary page, first, and ask for feedback on 
the rkward-devel mailing list, if in any doubt.

Regards
Thomas
